isolation_policy: bubblewrap mount namespace: only the workspace, the policy-accepted read allowlist and the opencode runtime exist; the repository, the other arms' results, the earlier sessions and the global opencode configuration (its MCP servers and plugins) are not mounted; plus the opencode v2 permission object (bash denied, edit and write denied, read and external_directory deny-by-default with the explicit allowlist)
limitations: The mount namespace is the filesystem guarantee; the model provider is reachable over the shared network, so a model that was shown a file can still send it away.
sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: gromovcrit-deepest-split
TITLE: A one-sigma prefix-confusion gate over a Gromov-delta cut certificate for behaviour-targeted splits of the deepest RQ-VAE SID level
MOTIVATION: The previous round executed a certificate-valid but coverage-first move set and edited about one third of the catalogue; the deep level of the SID therefore stopped being a stable refinement of the prefix and the validation L1 negative hit rate fell. The real failure mode of a generative recommender is not a badly partitioned catalogue, it is a small set of high-mass prefixes whose top-two deepest codes are statistically indistinguishable, so that the frozen Stage-3 model cannot commit to the correct continuation. Only those prefixes are worth editing, and only if the edit widens a geodesic decision margin.
NOVELTY: Unlike the earlier successor-Frechet codebook updates, per-level curvature control and behaviour-ranked radial assignment, this mechanism never touches the codebook, the curvature, the encoder or the training of Stage 2. It is a post-Stage-2 relabelling that changes only level L, and its new element is an ADMISSION TEST that a move must pass on top of the certificate: the move must touch a critical-confusion pair, defined by a one-Poisson-sigma band on the training-split top-two deepest-code counts for a frozen prefix, together with the condition that the competitor is the geodesically nearest competing code as seen from the prefix behaviour centroid. A move that merely preserves the hyperbolic tree structure is rejected unless it demonstrably sharpens a margin the frozen Stage-3 context actually has to resolve.
CHANGE: Successor transitions from the training split produce a Poincare successor barycentre per item and a prefix-conditional deepest-code confusion table; a critical-confusion set is extracted from that table by a one-sigma counting band; a curved split of the confusable code is proposed on the successor barycentres of only the successor items of critical prefixes; and the split is written into the SID table only if a Gromov-delta cut certificate holds on the split and the Poincare margin of every triggering critical prefix strictly increases.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Notation. L RQ levels; item i has code (k_1(i),...,k_L(i)) with prefix p(i) = (k_1(i),...,k_{L-1}(i)) frozen and bit-identical throughout. c_k in B^d is the frozen Stage-2 level-L centroid of code k, curvature kappa = -1, Poincare distance d_P, ball radius 1. z_i is the frozen Stage-2 item latent used by the deepest level. All statistics come from the training split only.\n1. Successor geodesic barycentre. With directed training counts A_ij, rowsum n_i = sum_j A_ij, training popularity pop_j:\n   w_ij = (A_ij / n_i) / sqrt(pop_j), renormalised to sum_j w_ij = 1 over j with A_ij > 0;\n   b_i = exp_0( sum_j w_ij * log_0(z_j) ), and b_i = z_i when n_i = 0.\n2. Prefix behaviour centroid. For prefix p with item set P_p, b_bar_p = exp_0( sum_{i in P_p} (n_i / sum_{i' in P_p} n_{i'}) * log_0(b_i) ).\n3. Prefix confusion table. For every training transition i -> j, increment N(p(i), k_L(j)). n_p = sum_k N(p,k). k1(p) = argmax, k2(p) = second largest in N.\n4. Critical set (THE ADDITIONAL PRECISION CONDITION). p is critical iff\n   (C1) N(p,k1) - N(p,k2) <= sqrt(N(p,k1))   [one-Poisson-sigma band; derived from the counts, sigma = 1 is the standard one-standard-error rule, not a swept constant]\n   (C2) k2 in argmin_{k != k1, N(p,k) > 0} d_P(b_bar_p, c_k)   [nearest competing code under the frozen Stage-2 geometry]\n   Base margin M0(p) = d_P(b_bar_p, c_k2) - d_P(b_bar_p, c_k1).\n5. Surgical move target. S* = { j : j is a successor under some critical p } intersect { j : k_L(j) = k1 }. Only items in S* may change their code; every other item keeps its code.\n6. Curved split proposal for code k1. m = Frechet mean of {b_i : k_L(i)=k1} (Karcher iteration, 5 steps). U = { i in S* : d_P(b_i, b_bar_p) < d_P(b_i, m) }. Seed m_a = Frechet mean of U, m_b = Frechet mean of S*\\U; run 3 alternating rounds of assignment by d_P and Frechet-mean update. Split k1 into k1' = the part whose centroid is geodesically nearer b_bar_p and k1'' = the other part, with centroids m' and m''.\n7. Certificate, split side (necessary, inherited in spirit from the previous round). With the metric induced by {b_i : i in S*}, Gromov product (x|y)_o = 0.5*(d_P(o,x)+d_P(o,y)-d_P(x,y)), o the ball origin, and cluster defect\n   delta_S = 0.5 * max_{x,y,z in S*} max(0, (x|y)_o - min((x|z)_o, (z|y)_o))   (deterministic index-stride sampling of triples when |S*| > 200),\nthe split is admissible iff\n   (S-a) d_P(m', m'') >= 2*max(rad(k1'), rad(k1'')), rad(X) = median_{i in X} d_P(b_i, m_X);\n   (S-b) delta_S - delta_{S after split} >= 0.5 * delta_S;\n   (S-c) cross-transition mass between the two parts <= median_{i in S*} sum_{j in S*} A_ij.\n8. Certificate, merge side. Two level-L codes ka, kb may be merged only if both are members of no critical pair, d_P(m_ka, m_kb) <= min(rad(ka), rad(kb)), the merged cluster defect is <= max(delta_ka, delta_kb), and the directed transition mass between them exceeds the within-median of clause (S-c). Merges exist to keep the level-L vocabulary size from growing and to make the both-off ablations well defined; a merge is executed only when the split budget has been exhausted.\n9. Execution rule. A split is written only if clauses (S-a),(S-b),(S-c) hold AND the margin rule M1(p) > M0(p) holds for every critical p that triggered it, with M1(p) = d_P(b_bar_p, m'') - d_P(b_bar_p, m'). Recompute the confusion table from step 3 and repeat, at most 3 rounds, stopping earlier when no move is admitted. Three is a fixed documented default, not a tuned value.\n10. Mandatory reporting (recorded, never used as a gate): moved fraction |{i : k_L changed}| / 24556; validation L1 negative hit rate before and after the edit; per-item deepest-code conditional entropy H(K_L | p) computed on training transitions, before and after, reported mass-weighted and for every touched prefix."}
COST: Zero added FLOPs per training step in both stages, because Stage 2 is already frozen and Stage 3 consumes the same SID tensor shape with different integers. The one-off edit dominates: at most 3 rounds over at most 24556 successor tokens, and within each round only the clusters S* of critical codes need pairwise Poincare distances (|S*| well under 10^3, so < 10^6 geodesic evaluations per round, < 3*10^6 total, each an O(d) log/exp-map evaluation). That is roughly 7*10^6/72000 = ~97 geodesic evaluations per frozen Stage-2 step amortised over 3000 epochs x 24 steps, i.e. wall clock minutes (2-6 min on one GPU, ~10 min on CPU) against hours for the 3000-epoch four-card Stage-2 run and the 150-epoch Stage 3, so under 1 percent of total wall clock. Memory: one dense successor row set plus the confusion table, O(nnz(A) + n_p * K_L) integers.
HYPOTHESIS: If the deepest-level loss is driven by genuine top-two confusion on high-mass prefixes rather than by noise, then a precision-first edit that touches only the successor items of one-sigma-indistinguishable prefixes will (i) move a small fraction of the catalogue, well below the previous one third, (ii) leave the validation L1 negative hit rate unchanged or better rather than degrading it, (iii) lower the deepest-code conditional entropy of the touched prefixes, and (iv) raise Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. Observed directly from the outputs of the single frozen Stage-3 run; if the moved fraction is small and recall does not move, the confusion hypothesis is falsified and the negative result is recorded with numbers.
RISKS: ['The critical set may be empty (over-precision), giving zero moves and a null result; Stage 3 conditions on the full L-level code so an improvement in the level-L margin may not alter its argmax; the successor barycentre is popularity-adjusted only to first order and may still be dominated by head items; Gromov-delta estimation on small S* is noisy and could admit a spurious cut; the training-split confusion ranking may not transfer to the test successor distribution; one seed means seed noise is inside the reported number.']
END IDEA

IDEA: HORO-TRANSPLANT-L
TITLE: Ideal-boundary horosphere transplant of the deepest RQ code, gated by a constant-free geodesic surprisal test against the frozen Stage-2 child anchors
MOTIVATION: The frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE assigns the deepest code k_L by residual nearest-neighbour in Euclidean space, so two items a user actually moves between in one session can sit under different deepest tokens while their L-1 prefixes agree. Stage 3 can only exploit a deepest-code improvement if the prefix it is conditioned on still points at that token; the previous round moved a third of the catalogue on a certificate that was necessary but not sufficient, and the validation L1 negative hit rate caught it. This idea repairs only the deepest level, and only where a curved membership test and a curved no-harm test agree, so the move set is small and every move is one the frozen prefix context can support.
NOVELTY: Prior rounds in this programme used (i) successor-weighted Frechet updates of codebook vectors, (ii) a per-level curvature scalar set by prefix-transition hardness, (iii) behaviour-ranked radial Poincare assignment with per-item curvature from context entropy. This mechanism uses none of those objects: it uses the IDEAL BOUNDARY of the Poincare ball (Busemann functions, horoballs), a purely negatively-curved construct with no Euclidean analogue that is neither a radius, nor a curvature scalar, nor a codebook mean; it acts after Stage 2 as a discrete transplant of the deepest code only, leaving levels 1..L-1 bit-identical; and its precision ingredient is a sign test on a geodesic surprisal DIFFERENCE, which contains no tunable constant.
CHANGE: Every item gets one hyperbolic Busemann height coordinate toward each sibling child cell's ideal boundary point; the destination child is chosen by training-split directed successor affinity, the item moves only if it lies inside that child's behaviour-implied horoball AND the move does not raise its geodesic distance to the child's frozen Stage-2 anchor relative to its current one, and only if a two-sided structural certificate holds.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Notation. N=24556 training items; frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE with L levels and per-level codebook size K (K_L children per parent); z_i the frozen encoder latent; SID(i)=(k_1..k_L); parent p(i)=(k_1..k_{L-1}); S_p={i: p(i)=p}; Ch_p={k_L(i): i in S_p}. Only k_L may change.\nStep 0 (behaviour, training split). M[i,j] = number of consecutive training-split pairs (u_t=i, u_{t+1}=j) over all training sessions, deduplicated per user so a repeated pair counts once per user. pop_i = number of training users who interacted with i.\nStep 1 (curved embedding, fixed curvature). Deterministic 4096-item training sample S0 (the 4096 smallest training item ids). s = median over ordered pairs of S0 of ||z_i - z_j||_2 / 2. x_i = exp_0(z_i/s) = tanh(||z_i/s||) * (z_i/s)/||z_i/s|| in the Poincare ball of radius 1, constant curvature K=-1; clip ||x_i|| <= 1-1e-3. d_H(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2||x-y||^2/((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))). s and the clip are derived, not tuned.\nStep 2 (child anchors, ideal boundary). For each parent p and k in Ch_p: m_{p,k} = Frechet mean of {x_i : i in S_p, k_L(i)=k} under d_H, by exactly 8 Riemannian gradient steps of size 1/8 from the Riemannian centroid (fixed, deterministic). xi_{p,k} = m_{p,k}/||m_{p,k}||; if ||m_{p,k}|| < 1e-6 fall back to x_j/||x_j|| for the highest-pop member j.\nStep 3 (Busemann / horosphere). B_{p,k}(x) = log((1-||x||^2)/(2||x-xi_{p,k}||^2)). Only differences of B are used, so its additive normalisation is irrelevant.\nStep 4 (behaviour-implied horosphere height, derived). Wbar[k->j] = (sum_{i in child k} M[i,j])/(pop_k pop_j); R_{p,k} = { j not in S_p : Wbar[k->j] > 0 }; h_{p,k} = median over j in R_{p,k} of B_{p,k}(x_j). Measured, no free constant.\nStep 5 (candidate for item i in child a). b(i) = argmax over k in Ch_p, k != a of sum_{j in child k} (M[i,j]+M[j,i])/sqrt(pop_i pop_j), ties by smallest code index. D_i = B_{p,b}(x_i) - h_{p,b} (>=0: inside b's behaviour-implied horoball). Delta_i = d_H(x_i,m_{p,b})^2 - d_H(x_i,m_{p,a})^2 (<=0: geodesic surprisal not increased).\nStep 6 (necessary two-sided certificate). Split side: |child a| >= 2 and i is not a cut vertex of the within-cell 1-NN behaviour graph G_a (nodes = members of child a, each node joined to its top-1 behaviour neighbour inside the cell, affinity as above, ties by item id); this keeps each deepest code's behaviour connectivity, which is what the frozen prefix was trained against. Merge side: b(i) already exists in Ch_p (no new code is created) and no child code of p is emptied by the batch.\nStep 7 (sufficiency gate, the new precision condition). Accept iff certificate passes AND D_i >= 0 AND Delta_i <= 0. Justification with no tuned constant: m_{p,k} are the frozen Stage-2 level-L code vectors carried into the ball by an isometry, so the frozen quantiser's preference for token k given prefix p is monotone decreasing in d_H(x_i, m_{p,k}); a move with Delta_i > 0 makes the item strictly less reachable by the frozen prefix-to-token map, so any behaviour-coherence gain cannot be realised at generation time. Delta_i <= 0 is the sign of a difference, hence the unique constant-free cut, and it is measured entirely from the training split and the frozen Stage-2 geometry.\nStep 8 (application). Exactly one synchronous pass per parent (no iteration: a fixed point is not guaranteed and would need a stopping constant). Accepted moves apply simultaneously; if the batch empties a child code of p, revert the single highest-pop moved-out item so the Stage-3 vocabulary set is unchanged. Report moved fraction, validation L1 negative hit rate before/after, per-item deepest-code conditional entropy before/after."}
COST: Essentially zero training cost. Stage 2 unchanged at 3000 epochs (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 72000 steps); Stage 3 unchanged at the frozen 150 epochs with unchanged vocabulary size. One offline pass between stages: per parent O(|S_p| * K * d) sibling affinities plus O(|S_p| * |Ch_p|) Busemann evaluations, total about 24556 * 256 * 64 ~= 4.0e8 multiply-adds plus one 1-NN graph, i.e. well under one CPU-minute; peak memory |S_p| * K floats because parents are streamed. Per-step added cost at the frozen scale: 0 flops on any of the 72000 Stage-2 steps and 0 on any Stage-3 step.
HYPOTHESIS: If the deepest code is where behaviour coherence is destroyed while the prefix context is still usable, a horosphere-gated transplant will lower per-item deepest-code conditional entropy for moved items, leave the validation L1 negative hit rate exactly unchanged, and push Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. Worth keeping if moved fraction is roughly 1-10%, entropy drops for moved items, and Recall@10 improves; refuted if a few percent move and Recall@10 is flat or worse, meaning the deepest level is not where the Stage-3 loss concentrates.
RISKS: ["The move set may be too small to shift Recall@10 (the deepest token carries only part of the generation loss). The monotone assumption behind Delta (Stage 3's prefix-to-child preference tracks geodesic distance to m_{p,k}) may fail, rejecting the moves that would help. Single-child parents, or parents whose children hold only singletons, contribute nothing. The 1-NN cut-vertex test is noisy on sparse low-popularity behaviour graphs. A pure label transplant with no codebook change can interact badly with an already-overfit Stage-3 last-token head."]
END IDEA

IDEA: GROMOV4-MARGIN-GATE-SID
TITLE: Measured-δ hyperbolic margin gate plus a training-demand gate for precision-first relabeling of the deepest RQ level
MOTIVATION: The frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE resolves the first L-1 tokens well but leaves the deepest token carrying almost no behavioural information: items whose training next-item demand differs sharply sit in the same (prefix, level-L) cell, so Stage 3 must memorise the tail of the SID instead of reading it off the tree. The earlier certificate round tried to fix this by moving one third of the catalogue on a predicate that was necessary but not sufficient, which redistributed the deepest codes without changing what Stage 3 actually has to emit and raised the validation L1 negative hit rate. This idea replaces coverage-first movement with a two-sided certificate whose tolerance is a *measured* hyperbolicity of the training transition graph and whose admissibility is additionally gated by training-split next-item demand, so that a move is only accepted when it changes the token Stage 3 must produce in a region where that token is genuinely uncertain.
NOVELTY: The occupied slots in this repository's history are: curved codebook update (Poincaré–Fréchet successor codebook), per-level curvature from a prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), radial behaviour-ranked assignment (BRad-RQ), Lorentz successor profiles, behaviour cones, geodesic boosts, MoE branch curvature, fibre mixtures. This idea touches none of them: both codebooks and levels 1..L-1 are frozen and bit-identical, the curvature is a single fixed value derived from the measured Gromov four-point defect of the training transition graph (not per level, not trained, not a radial coordinate), and the novel object is that the *same measured δ is re-expressed as a radius-dependent local hyperbolic resolution* δ_loc(i) which becomes the margin a discrete move must beat. The second novelty is the admissibility condition itself: a per-prefix deepest-token entropy gate and a per-item next-item-mass condition, both computed on the training split, which separate "satisfies the tree certificate" from "reduces what Stage 3 has to guess".
CHANGE: After the frozen Stage-2 run, each training item gets a hyperbolic point (exp map of its encoder embedding under a curvature fixed by the measured δ_G of the training transition graph), smoothed by a weighted Karcher mean over its training transition neighbours; each (prefix, deepest-code) cell gets a curved centroid. An item's deepest code is then reassigned inside its own prefix only if five inequalities hold simultaneously: a hyperbolic margin of one local δ, a transition-share advantage, a demand advantage, an entropy-eligible prefix, and a capacity cap taken from the frozen Stage-2 cell sizes. Stage 3 then runs unchanged on the relabelled SIDs.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'All quantities below are computed once after Stage 2, from the training split only, with a fixed seed 20261031; no gradient flows into SID construction; Stage 3 is then the single frozen 150-epoch run.\n(1) Symmetrised transition matrix W_ij = N_ij + N_ji from ordered training sessions; unweighted graph A = 1[W>0], giant weak component G.\n(2) Hop metric: BFS from a deterministic 2048-item sample S of G; δ_G = max over 262144 sampled quadruples (a,b,c,d) of (largest − second largest)/2 of {d_ab+d_cd, d_ac+d_bd, d_ad+d_bc}. Curvature c = 1/max(δ_G, 1.0), κ = −c².\n(3) 16 farthest-point-sampled anchors (seeded at the max-degree node); tangent vector v_i = s·(z_i − mean z) with s = median‖D_i‖ / median‖z_i − mean z‖ (D_i = the 16 hop distances). x_i = exp_0^κ(v_i) = tanh(c‖v_i‖)·v_i/(c‖v_i‖).\n(4) y_i = Riemannian weighted Karcher mean (20 fixed steps, step 1.0, retraction by exp) of {x_j : j ∈ {i} ∪ N32(i)} with ω_ii = 1 and ω_ij = W_ij/max_k W_ik.\n(5) Cell = (π_i, c_L(i)) with π_i = (c_1..c_{L-1})(i); m_cell = Karcher mean of {y_j : cell(j)=cell}.\n(6) Move predicate and greedy acceptance exactly as in SPEC EQUATIONS.'}
COST: Zero added cost inside training: 0 extra FLOPs on each of the 72,000 Stage-2 steps (24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs) and 0 on every Stage-3 step, because nothing is added to either loop — the mechanism is a one-shot post-Stage-2 construction whose output is a new deepest-token table. One-time precompute ≈ 2–4 CPU-minutes and <1 GB: 2048 BFS over ≈24.5k nodes and a few 10^5 edges (≈10^9 edge traversals, the dominant term), 262,144 quadruple evaluations (constant time each), 24,556 exp maps plus 24,556×20 Karcher retractions, a few thousand cell means, and a sparse T over at most 32 neighbours per item. Peak memory: 2048² float32 = 16 MB for the distance matrix, plus 24,556×64 float32 for the points. No GPU time, no retraining.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping only if three things hold in the single run: the moved fraction is materially smaller than the previous one third while still non-trivial (a few percent), the deepest-token conditional entropy falls under the entropy-eligible prefixes (the moves land where uncertainty was, not in already-well-predicted regions), and Stage-3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065. Observation is by direct comparison of the recorded before/after tables and the single test number; no arm is trained, so the case must be carried by the both-on run plus the pre-registered diagnostics.
RISKS: ['The training transition graph may be far from tree-like, giving a large δ_G, a small κ and a geometry almost indistinguishable from Euclidean; the behaviour graph may be too sparse to give most items a non-empty 32-neighbourhood, so almost nothing is admissible and the mechanism is inert; hyperbolic Karcher means shrink points toward the origin, which shortens all distances and could make the margin test too permissive; the median entropy gate could select prefixes that are high-entropy only because their cells are tiny; Stage 3 may be nearly insensitive to the deepest token (short SID, strong memorisation), in which case even a correct relabel cannot move recall; and the cap, anchored to frozen Stage-2 cell sizes, may block exactly the moves that matter when one cell is already dominant.']
END IDEA
